description: This topic explains the Islamic law of inheritance (Mirath or 'Ilm al-Faraid), its Qur'anic basis, what is done with the estate before distribution, the fixed shares of the main heirs, conditions that prevent inheritance, and the wisdom of the system.

mcq.questionText: What is the Islamic law that governs the distribution of a deceased person's wealth among the heirs called?
mcq.explanation: Mirath, also called 'Ilm al-Faraid (the science of fixed shares), is the branch of Islamic law that determines how a deceased person's estate is shared among the lawful heirs.

mcq.questionText: The detailed rules of fixed inheritance shares are mainly found in which Surah of the Qur'an?
mcq.explanation: The main verses giving the fixed shares of heirs are found in Surah an-Nisa (Chapter 4), which is why inheritance is described as an obligation set by Allah.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following must be paid FIRST from the estate, before the wealth is distributed to the heirs?

options.text: Funeral and burial expenses, then debts, then a valid bequest
Gifts to friends of the deceased
A new house for the wife

mcq.explanation: Before distribution, the estate is used to cover funeral and burial costs, then to pay off debts, then to carry out a valid bequest (wasiyyah) up to one-third. Only what remains is divided among the heirs.

mcq.questionText: What is the maximum portion of the estate that a person may give away through a wasiyyah (bequest)?
mcq.explanation: A wasiyyah may not exceed one-third of the estate, so that the lawful heirs are not deprived of their rightful shares.

mcq.questionText: A wasiyyah (bequest) normally may NOT be made to which of the following?

options.text: A person who is already a lawful heir

mcq.explanation: The general rule is 'no bequest to an heir', because the heir already receives a fixed share. A bequest is meant for those who would not otherwise inherit, such as charity or non-heir relatives.

mcq.questionText: When a man dies leaving sons and daughters, how do their shares compare?

options.text: Each son receives the same share as each daughter
Each son receives twice the share of each daughter
Each daughter receives twice the share of each son
Only the eldest son inherits everything

mcq.explanation: The Qur'an states that the male receives the share of two females in this situation, because in Islam the man carries the financial responsibility of maintaining the family.

mcq.questionText: A woman dies and is survived by her husband, but she has no children. What share does the husband receive?
mcq.explanation: A husband inherits one-half of his wife's estate when she leaves no children (or grandchildren). If she leaves children, his share is reduced to one-quarter.

mcq.questionText: A man dies and is survived by his wife and their children. What share does the wife receive?
mcq.explanation: A wife inherits one-eighth of her husband's estate when there are children. If there are no children, her share is one-quarter.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a condition that PREVENTS a person from inheriting?

options.text: Being a close relative of the deceased

mcq.explanation: A person who unlawfully kills the one from whom they would inherit is barred from inheritance, so that no one benefits from a crime. Difference of religion and slavery are the other classic barriers.

mcq.questionText: Besides killing, which of the following also prevents inheritance between two people in Sunni fiqh?

options.text: Difference of religion (e.g. a Muslim and a non-Muslim do not inherit from each other)

mcq.explanation: Difference of religion is a barrier to inheritance: a Muslim does not inherit from a non-Muslim and a non-Muslim does not inherit from a Muslim, according to mainstream Sunni rulings.

mcq.questionText: Why is it strongly recommended that a Muslim writes down debts owed and any bequest (wasiyyah)?

options.text: So that the heirs can ignore them
So that rights are protected and the estate is settled justly after death
Because writing increases the size of the estate
Because it cancels the need for funeral expenses

mcq.explanation: Writing down debts and a wasiyyah preserves people's rights, prevents disputes, and ensures the estate is divided correctly. A hadith advises a Muslim not to spend even two nights without having a written will ready.

mcq.questionText: If a deceased person leaves both a father and children, what is the father's basic fixed share?
mcq.explanation: When the deceased leaves children (or grandchildren), the father receives a fixed one-sixth of the estate. He may also take any remainder as a residuary heir in some cases.

mcq.questionText: If a deceased person leaves children, what is the mother's fixed share?
mcq.explanation: When the deceased leaves children (or two or more siblings), the mother's share is one-sixth. If there are no children and not many siblings, her share is one-third.

mcq.questionText: Which statement best describes the wisdom behind the Islamic inheritance system?

options.text: It allows the eldest son to take everything
It distributes wealth fairly among relatives and prevents it from being held by only one person
It encourages people to die without leaving a will
It gives wealth only to the rich relatives

mcq.explanation: Islamic inheritance spreads wealth among many relatives, prevents the concentration of wealth, maintains family ties, and protects the rights of the weak, including women and children.

mcq.questionText: A single daughter (with no sons present) inherits which fixed share of her parent's estate?
mcq.explanation: A single daughter (with no son to make her a residuary) receives a fixed one-half. Two or more daughters together (with no son) share two-thirds.

fib.questionText: The Islamic science of fixed inheritance shares is known in Arabic as 'Ilm al-_____.
fib.explanation: 'Ilm al-Faraid means the science of the fixed obligatory shares of inheritance.

fib.questionText: The main verses giving the fixed shares of heirs are found in Surah an-_____.
fib.explanation: Surah an-Nisa (Chapter 4) contains the detailed rules of inheritance.

fib.questionText: A bequest from a person's estate is called a _____ in Arabic.
fib.explanation: A wasiyyah is a will or bequest by which a person directs how part of their wealth should be used after death.

fib.questionText: A wasiyyah may not exceed one-_____ of the total estate.
fib.explanation: The bequest is limited to a maximum of one-third so that the heirs are not deprived.

fib.questionText: Before the estate is shared, funeral expenses and then the deceased's _____ must be paid.
fib.explanation: Debts owed by the deceased are settled before any inheritance is distributed.

fib.questionText: When a man dies leaving sons and daughters, each son receives _____ the share of each daughter.
fib.explanation: The Qur'an gives the male the share of two females in this case, in line with his duty to maintain the family.

fib.questionText: A wife inherits one-_____ of her husband's estate when he leaves children.
fib.explanation: The wife's share is one-eighth when there are children, and one-quarter when there are none.

fib.questionText: A husband inherits one-_____ of his wife's estate when she leaves children.
fib.explanation: The husband's share is one-quarter when there are children, and one-half when there are none.

fib.questionText: A person who deliberately _____ the one from whom he would inherit is barred from inheritance.
fib.explanation: Unlawful killing of the deceased prevents the killer from inheriting, so that no one benefits from a crime.

fib.questionText: Difference of _____ is a barrier to inheritance, so a Muslim and a non-Muslim do not inherit from each other.
fib.explanation: Difference of religion is one of the recognised barriers to inheritance in Sunni fiqh.

tf.questionText: The Islamic law of inheritance (Mirath) is based on the Qur'an and is an obligation set by Allah.
tf.explanation: Mirath is grounded in the Qur'an, especially Surah an-Nisa, and following it is a religious duty.

tf.questionText: Debts of the deceased should be paid only after the heirs have taken their shares.
tf.explanation: Debts are paid before distribution to the heirs. Only the remaining estate is divided.

tf.questionText: A person may leave a wasiyyah of up to one-third of the estate.
tf.explanation: The bequest is limited to a maximum of one-third of the estate.

tf.questionText: It is normally permitted to make a bequest (wasiyyah) to someone who is already a lawful heir.
tf.explanation: The rule is 'no bequest to an heir', because the heir already has a fixed share.

tf.questionText: A husband whose wife dies leaving no children inherits one-half of her estate.
tf.explanation: The husband receives one-half when there are no children, and one-quarter when there are.

tf.questionText: A wife always inherits the same fixed share whether or not her husband leaves children.
tf.explanation: Her share changes: one-quarter when there are no children, and one-eighth when there are.

tf.questionText: A person who unlawfully kills the deceased is prevented from inheriting from them.
tf.explanation: Killing the one from whom you would inherit is a barrier to inheritance.

tf.questionText: In Sunni fiqh, a Muslim can inherit from a non-Muslim relative and vice versa without any restriction.
tf.explanation: Difference of religion is a barrier; a Muslim and a non-Muslim do not inherit from one another.

tf.questionText: A single daughter (with no son present) inherits a fixed one-half of her parent's estate.
tf.explanation: One daughter alone takes one-half; two or more daughters together share two-thirds.

tf.questionText: Writing down debts and a will helps protect people's rights and reduce disputes after death.
tf.explanation: Recording debts and a wasiyyah preserves rights and helps the estate be settled justly.

summary.questionText: Define Mirath ('Ilm al-Faraid) in one sentence.
summary.correctAnswer: Mirath, or 'Ilm al-Faraid, is the Islamic law that determines how a deceased person's wealth is divided among the lawful heirs in fixed shares set by Allah.
summary.explanation: It is the science of the fixed obligatory shares of inheritance based mainly on the Qur'an.

summary.questionText: List, in order, the things that must be done with the estate before it is distributed to the heirs.
summary.correctAnswer: First pay funeral and burial expenses, then pay the deceased's debts, then carry out a valid bequest (wasiyyah) up to one-third; the remainder is then shared among the heirs.
summary.explanation: This order ensures obligations and rights are settled before inheritance is divided.

summary.questionText: What is a wasiyyah, and what are its two main limits?
summary.correctAnswer: A wasiyyah is a bequest from one's estate; it must not exceed one-third of the estate and must not normally be given to a lawful heir.
summary.explanation: These limits protect the rights of the heirs.

summary.questionText: State the husband's two possible shares and when each applies.
summary.correctAnswer: The husband takes one-half if his wife leaves no children, and one-quarter if she leaves children.
summary.explanation: The presence of children reduces the husband's share.

summary.questionText: State the wife's two possible shares and when each applies.
summary.correctAnswer: The wife takes one-quarter if her husband leaves no children, and one-eighth if he leaves children.
summary.explanation: The presence of children reduces the wife's share.

summary.questionText: How do the shares of a son and a daughter compare, and why?
summary.correctAnswer: A son receives twice the share of a daughter because in Islam the man bears the financial responsibility of maintaining the family.
summary.explanation: The larger male share is balanced by the male's duty of maintenance.

summary.questionText: Name three conditions that prevent a person from inheriting.
summary.correctAnswer: Difference of religion, unlawfully killing the deceased, and slavery are the classic barriers to inheritance.
summary.explanation: These barriers stop inheritance even between close relatives.

summary.questionText: Give three points showing the wisdom and fairness of the Islamic inheritance system.
summary.correctAnswer: It distributes wealth among many relatives, prevents the concentration of wealth in one person, protects the rights of women and children, and helps maintain family ties.
summary.explanation: The system spreads wealth justly and safeguards the weak.

summary.questionText: Why is it important to write down one's debts and bequest?
summary.correctAnswer: Writing them down protects people's rights, prevents disputes among heirs, and ensures the estate is settled justly; a hadith encourages keeping a written will ready.
summary.explanation: Clear records make a fair and peaceful settlement possible.

summary.questionText: State the fixed share of the mother when the deceased leaves children, and when she leaves no children or many siblings.
summary.correctAnswer: The mother takes one-sixth when the deceased leaves children (or two or more siblings), and one-third when there are no children and not many siblings.
summary.explanation: Her share depends on the presence of children and siblings.

hoq.questionText: A man dies leaving an estate of 240,000 shillings after debts and expenses. He is survived by his wife and several children. The wife takes one-eighth. How much does the wife receive?
hoq.explanation: The wife's share is one-eighth because there are children: 240,000 / 8 = 30,000 shillings.

hoq.questionText: A woman dies leaving a net estate of 60,000 shillings. She is survived by her husband only, with no children and no other heirs. The husband takes one-half as a fixed share. How much does the husband receive in total (assuming he then also takes the remainder as the only heir)?
hoq.explanation: With no children, the husband's fixed share is one-half (30,000). As the only surviving heir, the remaining one-half returns to him by radd/residue, so he effectively receives the whole 60,000 shillings.

hoq.questionText: A man dies leaving a net estate of 90,000 shillings, survived by one son and one daughter only. A son receives twice the share of a daughter. How much does the son receive?
hoq.explanation: Divide the estate into 3 parts (2 for the son, 1 for the daughter): 90,000 / 3 = 30,000. The son receives 2 parts = 60,000 shillings and the daughter 1 part = 30,000 shillings.
